newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm, more gains seen.
newsitem.headline: SIMEX Nikkei futures end firm, more gains seen.

text.p: SIMEX Nikkei futures ended higher on active turnover on Monday and dealers said the market showed potential for further gains though players were likely to be cautious ahead of a key business sentiment survey.
The benchmark Nikkei 225 December contract ended 85 points above its previous close at 21,215, after touching a high of 21,420.
"It appears there's more upside potential. There'll be minor resistance at 21,420, but I foresee it going up to 21,550 tomorrow," said a chartist with a local institution.
He said the December Nikkei could then undergo a mild correction, but was likely to remain supported at 21,300, which was previously a strong resistance level.
Longer-term resistance is seen at 21,650 and 21,845.
Dealers said the December Nikkei was underpinned by gains on the cash market on Monday.
A Japanese bank dealer said the market would keep a close watch on the Bank of Japan (BOJ)'s quarterly tankan, due on Wednesday, for an indication of further direction.

"If the tankan shows negative numbers, that will definitely start the talk of the Japanese government increasing fiscal spending again. That would be positive for the Nikkei but bad for JGBs (Japanese government bonds)," he said.
